newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic in robotic surgery system marketing deal.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic in robotic surgery system marketing deal.

text.p: Medtronic Inc and Computer Motion Inc agreed to collaborate on promoting Computer Motion's computer-assisted robotic systems for minimally invasive cardiac surgery, the companies said.

Medtronic will be exclusive distributor of the systems in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and co-marketer in the United States and Canada after the products undergo clinical testing and receive regulatory approvals, they said.
Medtronic has invested an undisclosed amount in Computer Motion, as well, the companies said.
The Computer Motion system for cardiothoracic surgery, named Zeus, is expected to be commercially available in 1998, the companies said.

Zeus is a computer- and voice-controlled robotic system that positions and maneuvers an endoscope and instruments for performing microsurgical procedures through small incisions made between a patient's ribs.

Zeus enables a new endoscopic surgical procedure called E-CABG, for endoscopic coronary artery bypass graft, which allows multiple occluded coronary arteries to be bypassed without the thoracotomy or mini-thoracotomy now used.
"Elimination of these larger surgical incisions is expected to result in faster recovery times, less hospitalization, and over-all lower costs," they said.
